title: Imagene AI infers EGFR mutation from an H&E slide, letting a woman with leptomeningeal lung cancer start osimertinib two days after biopsy and avoid neuraxis radiotherapy
summary: Imagene AI predicted EGFR from an H&E slide in <48 h; rapid PCR confirmed; osimertinib began 2 days post-biopsy, no neuraxis radiotherapy.
account: In July 2022 (day not given; first day used) a healthy woman in her early 40s was admitted to Tel Aviv Sourasky Medical Center, Tel Aviv, Israel, with a month of worsening headaches; imaging showed a 2.6 cm left apical lung adenocarcinoma with leptomeningeal spread, and biopsy tissue was scarce. To guide gene testing without exhausting tissue, the team ran Imagene's deep-learning algorithm on the H&E slide; within 48 hours of biopsy it inferred EGFR mutation positivity. A rapid Idylla PCR assay confirmed the L858R exon 21 mutation and osimertinib started two days after biopsy, which the authors state was one week earlier than routine practice and avoided whole-neuraxis radiotherapy. MRI after two months showed disappearance of the enhancement.
purpose: Imagene's algorithm is built to infer genomic alteration status from routine pathology slides in order to direct molecular testing; this benefit is its intended function.
segment: AI-guided biomarker testing in non-small-cell lung cancer
taxonomy_note: Good fit: the gain was a shorter, tissue-sparing molecular workflow that moved targeted therapy forward by a week.

ratings.reason: Targeted therapy for leptomeningeal disease started a week earlier and whole-neuraxis radiotherapy was avoided, with MRI improvement at two months; survival benefit is not reported.
The slide-based inference let the team choose a single rapid PCR test instead of waiting for sequencing on limited tissue.

ai_role.statement: The AI inference directed which rapid test to run; treatment began only after PCR confirmation. The AI therefore changed the sequence and speed of testing rather than the final diagnosis. Authors are Tel Aviv Sourasky / Tel Aviv University clinicians declaring no competing interests; a second patient in the report (February 2023) followed the same path.
